newsitem.title: USA: Polaris comfortable with 1997 EPS range.
newsitem.headline: Polaris comfortable with 1997 EPS range.

text.p: Polaris Industries Inc expects 1997 earnings per share in line with the range of analysts' estimates, the company's chief financial officer said Thursday.
"The range the Street has (for 1997 EPS) is $2.40 to $2.45, and we're comfortable with that range," Michael Malone told Reuters before the company's annual shareholder meeting.
According to First Call, analysts' 1997 earnings estimates range from $2.35 to $2.46 a share. The consensus is $2.42.

Malone said the personal recreation vehicle manufacturer would continue repurchasing shares as part of a program approved in January. To date the company has repurchased 1.4 million of the three million shares authorized for buyback.
"We're encouraged to see (the stock price) at $29 to $30 a share, but we're still actively buying," Malone said.
He said Polaris expects all-terrain vehicle (ATV) sales to rise in 1997.
"We expect retail ATV sales to increase in the lower double-digit range in percent growth year over year," he said.
However, he said Polaris 1997 snowmobile sales would decline, while industry-wide snowmobile sales are expected to be flat.
"Orders are down, as we anticipated, but they're down in a range that's acceptable," he said.
Polaris will launch in spring of 1998 its Victory motorcycle line.
"The financial breakeven point is three years on the $20 million investment," the line's general manager, Matthew Parks, told shareholders.
